editorial:
Imagine waking up in a creepy mental hospital with no idea how you got there, only to find out you are accused of burning down a house. You play along with Kristen, a scared girl who quickly realizes that the other patients are disappearing one by one. The vibe is super eerie and feels like a bad dream where nothing is quite what it seems. You will spend most of the movie wondering if the doctors are evil or if Kristen is just losing her mind. It creates a great sense of dread that keeps you guessing about the real danger lurking in the halls.

What really works here is the big twist and the way the tension builds up. While some parts feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it if you love mysteries. It is a solid pick for a rainy night. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the dark details, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you are a fan of old-school horror style.
endingExplained: You find out that Kristen is not actually in a hospital at all. The entire place is a dream inside her own head. She is actually in a coma after the fire she started. The ghost chasing her is a version of herself. To wake up, she has to fight her own mind and accept the truth. Once she does this, she finally wakes up in a real hospital bed in the real world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves twist endings and creepy hospitals.
